telos.statement: Determine whether Loom truthfully supports arbitrary one-edge multi-model conversation, exact observable context, durable execution, and the governed German workflow without losing personal-operational-graph provenance.

owner_claims.statement: Every invocation must answer what exact world the agent was shown and name provider-owned proof limits.
The user experiences a live conversation with routing powers rather than a workflow IDE.

owner_sources.excerpt: Loom is a local-first conversational lattice harness: a user progressively authors a graph of model invocations, one consequential edge at a time, while retaining exact control over what each invocation receives, which model performs it, what tools it may use, and how its output becomes available to later work.

The user experiences a live conversation with routing powers, not a workflow IDE. The system underneath may be an orchestrator, but the foreground interaction is a friendly, slow-motion macro-Loom in which the next edge is visible and steerable.

findings.title: Exact-context claims exceed what is validated and shown
findings.claim: Context selections can label verbatim bytes as summarized and cite nonexistent derivation blocks, while the cockpit never renders its compiled_prompt_preview and sealed invocation inspection omits exact prompt bytes and attempt-level CLI identity.
findings.failure_mode: A manifest can be internally hash-consistent while asserting false transformation lineage; the operator sees labels and hashes rather than the actual world sent.
findings.consequence: The central promise—knowing exactly what each agent saw—can be confidently but incorrectly believed.
findings.response: Require typed transformation receipts with resolving parents; independently validate every selected and omitted source; expose exact compiled bytes and runtime influence receipts in the cockpit. The control remains implemented, its permanent regression passes at the frozen revision, and the finding remains in lineage rather than disappearing.

findings.title: Subscription-only execution is not enforced by the child environment
findings.claim: The environment filter removes names containing a few secret markers but preserves backend selectors, cloud credentials, and provider base URLs that can route official CLIs through developer-billed surfaces.
findings.failure_mode: A machine configured for Bedrock, Vertex, or a custom provider endpoint can execute a Loom invocation outside the promised consumer subscription without Loom recording the authority change.
findings.consequence: Private prompts may cross an undeclared billing and trust boundary, invalidating the execution contract across providers.
findings.response: Construct an explicit minimal child environment and provider-specific consumer-auth allowlist; reject backend selector and developer-cloud state with permanent mutation tests. The control remains implemented, its permanent regression passes at the frozen revision, and the finding remains in lineage rather than disappearing.

findings.title: Workflow packs are declarations without an enforcing engine
findings.claim: Allowed transitions, triggers, closure rules, role routes, and context-module modes are validated as JSON but are never consumed by a runtime state machine.
findings.failure_mode: The quaternary pack can claim automatic blinded challenge and frozen-query gates while Loom permits unrelated actions and performs none of those transitions automatically.
findings.consequence: The first complete German workflow and any later workflow pack cannot inherit their declared epistemic guarantees from Loom.
findings.response: Compile packs into an executable transition/trigger machine; block undeclared transitions; attach required contexts; generate challenger invocations and authority receipts from canonical state. The control remains implemented, its permanent regression passes at the frozen revision, and the finding remains in lineage rather than disappearing.

findings.title: External workflow writes have no durable idempotency boundary
findings.claim: Workflow command POSTs invoke gatherctl without a lease or idempotency key, then persist only a hash receipt after the external command returns.
findings.failure_mode: A lost response or process failure after the quaternary database mutates can cause a retry to repeat the write; the exact returned object is not preserved as a Loom artifact.
findings.consequence: Canonical quaternary state and Loom history can diverge precisely at the authority boundary the workflow exists to govern.
findings.response: Add generation-bound command intents, leases, stable idempotency keys accepted by the authoritative writer, durable result bytes, and reconciliation for unknown outcomes. The control remains implemented, its permanent regression passes at the frozen revision, and the finding remains in lineage rather than disappearing.

findings.title: The append-only ledger cannot rebuild its derived state
findings.claim: Events omit the full manifests, context provenance, role authority, attempts, and slice bodies required to reconstruct current tables, and no replay/rebuild path exists.
findings.failure_mode: Restart works only because mutable derived tables survive; corruption or a future migration cannot recover the lattice from the claimed append-only truth.
findings.consequence: A broad storage fault invalidates the durable-history guarantee and leaves no independent canonical recovery path.
findings.response: Either make complete versioned events canonical with deterministic rebuild, or explicitly make immutable object tables canonical and narrow the ledger claim; prove fresh-database replay equivalence. The control remains implemented, its permanent regression passes at the frozen revision, and the finding remains in lineage rather than disappearing.

findings.title: Provider artifacts disappear after successful execution
findings.claim: The response schema requires artifacts, but the supervisor reads only payload.response; artifact rows, blocks, edges, and inspector data are never created.
findings.failure_mode: A successful provider can return a cited file or structured proof and Loom silently discards it while marking the attempt succeeded.
findings.consequence: Downstream joins and workflow evidence cannot consume or inspect one of the invocation contract’s promised outputs.
findings.response: Persist each artifact with exact bytes, media type, lineage, produced edges, and inspector exposure before terminal success. The control remains implemented, its permanent regression passes at the frozen revision, and the finding remains in lineage rather than disappearing.

findings.title: Trailheads are roots rather than branch tips
findings.claim: The query excludes invocations that have parent edges, selecting nodes with no parents; the edge orientation is child source to parent target, so leaf trailheads are omitted.
findings.failure_mode: After one follow-up the cockpit offers the initial invocation as the continuation point instead of the live tip.
findings.consequence: Ordinary conversational steering branches from the wrong place unless the user manually finds and checks history.
findings.response: Select invocations that are not the target of any child-to-parent inheritance edge and regression-test forks and joins. The control remains implemented, its permanent regression passes at the frozen revision, and the finding remains in lineage rather than disappearing.

findings.title: Ordinary role creation leaves orphan context on failure
findings.claim: create_role commits the instruction context block in one transaction and inserts the role in a later transaction; a duplicate role name leaves the first write durable.
findings.failure_mode: Validation or uniqueness failures create invisible, unreferenced private blocks and events despite the operation reporting failure.
findings.consequence: Repeated mistakes pollute the canonical lattice and make failed operations observably non-atomic.
findings.response: Move dependent object creation into one transaction with prewritten content-addressed bytes and add failure-stage mutations for bootstrap and draft creation. The control remains implemented, its permanent regression passes at the frozen revision, and the finding remains in lineage rather than disappearing.

closure_claims.statement: The append-only Loom ledger, blob store, reconstruction path, leases, and restart reconciliation preserve sealed invocation history across process loss.
Every sealed invocation exposes independently reconstructed compiled context, observable runtime influence receipts, and exact response and artifact bytes.
Official subscription CLI routes enforce role, origin, environment, tool, lease, and terminal-state boundaries without developer-credential fallback.
The one-edge operations support invoke, fork, join, inspect, diff, replay, tag, and extract while preserving typed graph ancestry and trailheads.
Typed workflow packs enforce initial state, reachability, role routes, trigger actions, deterministic commands, and visible recovery without absorbing domain authority.
The response-first cockpit distinguishes failure, unavailable routes, exact context, governed actions, and safely rendered model output from legitimate empty state.
Slate and Axial consume bounded Loom projections only after independently resolving identity, revision, coverage, safety, and stale-edge semantics.

residuals.statement: The Loom Surface census covers the Loom workframe; model-runner, Slate, and Axial integration files are separately full-file hash-inspected by this audit rather than recursively represented in that Surface.

The complete authenticated German native-role acceptance remains unavailable because Gemini CLI 0.45.0 rejects the consumer tier and cannot satisfy Loom's exact-context isolation contract; workflow machinery is verified, but full German closure is not claimed.
Official provider CLIs do not expose every provider-owned system instruction or server-side transformation; manifests name this opacity and claim only locally observable inputs and influences.

The rendered acceptance used seeded local results and did not repeat authenticated Claude or Codex spend on the exact frozen revision; prior authenticated local journals remain historical evidence rather than exact-revision acceptance.
